title: Q3 → Q4 Sales Overview: Resin Pricing Drives a 14% Margin Lift
summary: Resin product revenue grew 18% quarter-over-quarter while unit shipment volumes stayed flat, driven primarily by a 12% price lift in LDPE grades. PC grades underperformed against plan by 9% on softening export demand, partially offset by stronger PVC pricing in the domestic market.
methodology: Aggregated from erp_product_sales_details (fact table joined to dim_product). Filters: FY26 Q3+Q4, sales org = Z01, currency = RMB. Top-8 by shipment_volume; rebalanced for grade-level margin to surface the resin / PC divergence.

slides.title: Resin pricing masked weaker PC grades
bullets: Resin pricing added ¥112M of gross margin vs. flat volumes, masking weaker PC grades.
PC grade export volume fell 14% QoQ; softer EU demand is the proximate cause.
Top-3 SKUs (LDPE Film, LLDPE Rotation, PVC Pipe) account for 28% of revenue; concentration is up.
Freight cost re-negotiation adds an estimated ¥22M of FY26 cushion.
OTIF misses plan by 0.9pt; root cause is concentrated at 2 plants (Shanghai, Tianjin).
Backlog at ¥312M (+7% QoQ) gives some forward-cover against the PC softness.

slides.title: Five things worth your attention
bullets: Resin grades (LDPE + LLDPE) drove 71% of margin expansion, even though they represent only 38% of volume.
PVC domestic pricing benefited from tighter spot-market supply in July; sustaining it is the upside risk.
PC export softness tracks softening EU appliance demand — not likely to reverse before CY27.
Top-customer concentration rose to 41% (vs. 38% prior quarter); worth a diversification play.
Freight cost per ton fell 6% on renegotiated rail contracts; an extra ¥22M of cushion.

slides.title: Decisions we want from S&OP this week
bullets: Re-weight Oct–Dec plan toward resin grades to capture pricing upside; pause PC export push.
Diversify top-customer exposure — start renewal talks with #6–#10 accounts now.
Rebid the Shanghai + Tianjin OTIF root-cause (joint with S&OP) by end of September.
Lock in freight cost savings as a recurring line in the FY27 budget.
